decisions.rationale: "Lesch-Nyhan" is a disease name used adjectivally to modify the noun "patient" in the title ("a Lesch-Nyhan patient"), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 - Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: "disease" in "probably cause disease" is a very general term with no specific disease identified, so it is excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §4 - Do not annotate general terms

decisions.rationale: "Lesch-Nyhan syndrome" is a named disease with one specific definition and no further categorization, used as the subject of the sentence.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: "complete deficiency of hypoxanthine guanine phosphoribosyltransferase" names a specific enzyme deficiency (complete HPRT deficiency) that defines a single disease condition, not the generic term 'deficiency' alone; it is therefore annotated as a Specific Disease, though this is a borderline case.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Specific Disease mentions; What NOT to Annotate §4 (general 'deficiency' exclusion does not apply to a fully specified condition)

decisions.rationale: "Lesch-Nyhan syndrome" appears as the named disease in the prepositional complement "patient with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome", referring to the disease itself rather than acting as an adjectival modifier, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: "HPRT deficient" is a disease description used adjectivally to modify "patients" ("HPRT deficient patients"), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
